# Sunplus SPCA2281 / XWF-1080P camera test

Manual test on November 4, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles), against Joshua commit
`74ecbcc618658358de2bbc9048fe9d60df7acadb`. This records the camera run performed
while adding the [Sunplus preset](../../../config/config_preset/example/sunplus_spca2281.pbtxt).
It is a short test of one unit, not an endurance or model-wide qualification.

## Setup and procedure

- USB product description: `Sunplus Innovation Technology Inc. SPCA2281 Web Camera`.
- V4L2 product: `XWF-1080P: XWF-1080P`; capture node `/dev/video0`.
- Ubuntu 22.04 / ROS 2 Humble / x86_64 in the Joshua Docker environment.
- Ran `//ros2:camera_publisher` directly with node name `sunplus_camera_publisher`,
  node ID `1`, and the Sunplus preset. No actuator or board node was launched.
- Used ROS domain `114` and `ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1`.
- Subscribed to `/sunplus_camera/image_raw` with a reliable rclpy subscription,
  depth 10, for a 12-second observation window including startup and discovery.
- Counted received messages using the subscriber's monotonic receipt times.
  Validated dimensions, encoding, and payload length, and saved a sample frame.
- Separately ran Joshua's `//ros2/utils:camera_subscriber` desktop preview and
  confirmed that it received and displayed images. Capture was stopped afterward.

The publisher's successful initialization log reported 640x480 and a negotiated
30 FPS. The observed message rate below is measured separately; negotiating a
rate does not establish that the device delivers it.

## Retained result summary

```json
{
  "received_frames": 91,
  "duration_seconds": 10.634,
  "measured_fps": 8.46,
  "width": 640,
  "height": 480,
  "encoding": "rgb8",
  "step": 1920,
  "bytes_per_frame": 921600,
  "byte_min": 0,
  "byte_max": 255,
  "topic": "/sunplus_camera/image_raw",
  "subscriber_qos": "reliable",
  "requested_fps": 30
}
```

The configured capture format was MJPG; initialization applied it successfully.
A V4L2 format query during an earlier run also confirmed MJPG at 640x480.
Direct OpenCV comparisons at 640x480, requesting 30 FPS with a one-frame buffer,
captured 60 frames in 7.444 seconds with MJPG and 7.338 seconds with YUYV.
These measurements establish that the low capture rate also occurred outside
Joshua; they do not establish its underlying cause.

The config preset validation and perception factory tests passed in the Humble
Docker environment. They establish software checks separately from this manual
hardware evidence. Camera frames are not committed because they contain imagery
from the local environment; this document retains the measured summary.

## Scope and reproduction

Only 640x480 capture and RGB ROS output were verified. Although the camera
advertised larger modes, including 1920x1080, those modes were not exercised.
Jazzy, other hardware revisions, synchronization accuracy, and sustained
30 FPS operation were not verified.

For a new run, follow the [hardware rules](../../../AGENTS.md#hardware-safety--read-this-first),
confirm the camera's capture index, build the publisher and viewer in the
matching Docker environment, and run the same preset. The preset remains the
configuration source of truth. A historical test does not establish that the
currently connected device is ready or grant permission to open it.

limitations: Short capture and desktop preview on one physical unit; no endurance or cross-platform qualification.
Requested 30 FPS; measured 8.46 FPS with a reliable ROS subscriber. Direct OpenCV capture also achieved approximately 8 FPS.
1080p capture was not tested. The model name and advertised modes are not verification evidence.
The preset uses camera index 0; resolve the connected device before running because indices can change.
USB VID:PID and model aliases identify a candidate model, not a unique physical unit or a guarantee for every hardware revision.

# Sunplus SPCA2281 / XWF-1080P: sustained 1080p capture

Manual test on November 4, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles). Joshua delivered
1920x1080 RGB images at approximately 30 FPS for a 300-second measurement window.
This result uses an optimized build and the two-buffer capture fix described
below. It does not qualify every build mode, hardware revision, or environment.

## Source and setup

- Source base: `261887dfdcfd9645b846ecffe3a3f30cfb3f111b`.
- The test tree additionally changed `CvCamera` from one capture buffer to two
  and added the [1080p preset](../../../config/config_preset/example/sunplus_spca2281_1080p.pbtxt).
  Those changes were uncommitted during the run; the base commit alone does not
  contain the tested buffer setting or preset.
- Tested driver SHA-256:
  `f3ede40449aee042d16d68a683a7efd6668e9e602d5da7216aa1805b98201fe2`.
- Tested preset SHA-256:
  `27cd16f5d8eb0a130799728e459cdd586ea3eca2ca59473da708c6c818916b3a`.
- Ubuntu 22.04 / ROS 2 Humble / x86_64 in the Joshua Docker environment.
- Build flags: `-c opt --config=u22 --config=x86-base` and
  `--@rules_python//python/config_settings:python_version=3.10`.
- Only the standalone camera publisher and a measurement subscriber ran. No
  actuator, board, or robot preset was launched.
- The camera's original automatic-exposure settings were used throughout the
  final run. A separate temporary manual-exposure diagnostic did not improve
  the single-buffer rate; its settings were restored before qualification.

## Measurement procedure

The camera advertised 1920x1080 MJPG at 30 FPS and YUYV at 5 FPS. The test used
MJPG and verified the active format, dimensions, and negotiated 30 FPS through
V4L2 while the publisher was running. Negotiation was checked separately from
the measured delivery rate.

Ran `//ros2:camera_publisher` with node ID `1` and the 1080p preset. A reliable
rclpy subscriber with depth 10 read `/sunplus_camera/image_raw` on a loopback-only
ROS domain. After a five-second warmup from the first received message, it
counted messages for exactly 300 seconds using monotonic receipt times.

Every received frame was checked for width 1920, height 1080, encoding `rgb8`,
row stride 5760, and payload length 6220800 bytes. The measurement retained
receipt intervals, publisher timestamps, and counts in consecutive 10-second
windows. A final image was saved locally; camera imagery is not committed.

Before the run, the acceptance criteria were set to mean delivery of at least
29.5 FPS, at least 29 FPS in every full 10-second window, no receipt gap above
100 ms, no invalid frame metadata/payload lengths, and strictly increasing
publisher timestamps. These criteria verify approximately 30 FPS delivery for
this finite run, not sensor-level exposure timing or loss-free acquisition.

## Results

| Measurement | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Measurement window | 300 seconds, following a five-second warmup |
| Frames received | 9001 |
| Mean delivery rate | 30.003333 FPS |
| Rate from publisher timestamp span | 30.002796 FPS |
| Lowest / highest 10-second window | 29.9 / 30.1 FPS |
| Longest receipt gap | 56.313 ms |
| 99th percentile receipt gap | 46.064 ms |
| Invalid frame metadata or payload lengths | 0 |
| Repeated or decreasing publisher timestamps | 0 |
| Acceptance criteria | Passed |

All 30 individual window rates are retained in the
[structured test record](../../hardware_test_records.json). The publisher remained
active throughout measurement and was stopped afterward; the camera was released
and its original exposure settings were confirmed. An empty-frame warning
coincided with SIGINT during shutdown, after the measurement window; it was not
an outage during the timed run.

## Diagnosing the initial frame-rate limit

| Short comparison | Frames / duration | Measured rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original Joshua development build, one buffer | 153 / 10 seconds | 15.3 FPS |
| Direct OpenCV, automatic exposure, one buffer | 123 / 8.032 seconds | 15.313 FPS |
| Direct OpenCV, temporary manual exposure, one buffer | 120 / 8.000 seconds | 15.000 FPS |
| Direct OpenCV, one buffer, JPEG decoding disabled | 97 / 6.032 seconds | 16.081 FPS |
| Direct OpenCV, two buffers, JPEG decoded | 180 / 6.000 seconds | 29.999 FPS |
| Direct OpenCV, four buffers, JPEG decoded | 181 / 6.030 seconds | 30.014 FPS |
| Joshua development build, two buffers | 232 / 10 seconds | 23.2 FPS |
| Joshua optimized build, two buffers | 301 / 10 seconds | 30.1 FPS |

Two capture buffers let the driver keep the next frame queued while the
previous buffer is dequeued. The comparisons demonstrate that a single buffer
limited this setup, and that the development build remained slower than the
optimized build. The 300-second run above is the sustained qualification.

## Reproduction and scope

Follow the [hardware rules](../../../AGENTS.md#hardware-safety--read-this-first) and
confirm the camera's capture index before running. Inside a Joshua Docker
development shell, use the tested two-buffer driver and run:

```sh
bazel run -c opt --config=u22 --config=x86-base \
  --@rules_python//python/config_settings:python_version=3.10 \
  //ros2:camera_publisher -- sunplus_1080p_publisher 1 \
  config/config_preset/example/sunplus_spca2281_1080p.pbtxt
```

Use a reliable subscriber on the image topic to repeat the timed procedure;
the camera's advertised or negotiated rate alone is insufficient. This run
does not qualify Jazzy, other lighting conditions, longer operation, camera
exposure timestamps, or other hardware revisions.

limitations: A five-minute run on one physical unit and one Ubuntu 22.04/Humble setup; not an endurance or cross-platform qualification.
This result requires the two-buffer capture change and an optimized build. With two buffers, the default development build measured 23.2 FPS in the short comparison.
The recorded Joshua commit is the source base; the driver change and new preset were uncommitted during measurement. Their exact SHA-256 hashes are retained in the environment.
Frame rate and gaps were measured at the ROS subscriber. Publisher timestamps do not establish camera-exposure timing, synchronization accuracy, or delivery of every sensor exposure.
The final automatic-exposure settings matched the original settings. Other lighting conditions and hardware revisions were not qualified.
